title: Optimistic decode operator: routing telemetry, acceptance scoring, and controlled fallthrough
creator: Sara Kim
description:
Background: We want a low-latency fast-path for decode using optimistic (speculative) decoding that tries a cheaper / faster model or kernel and falls back if acceptance signals are weak. This ticket implements an "optimistic decode operator" in the runtime that: routes short prefill probes, computes real-time acceptance scores, emits structured telemetry, and performs deterministic controlled fallthrough to safe variants (model or kernel) when probes indicate risk.

Goals: Improve median decode latency for conversational traffic by ~15-25% for compatible inputs while keeping quality regression <= 0.5% measured on our eval prompt set. Provide clear telemetry to quantify: probe accept rate, wasted tokens cost, fallback frequency, and end-to-end latency delta. Ship runbook and automated rollouts with safety gates.

Scope: runtime operator + routing policy, telemetry schema, rollout plan, unit+integration tests, console dashboard hooks. NOT in scope: end-user API changes, new model quantization (handled by separate task).
acceptance_criteria: Optimistic operator can route a prefill probe to a fast kernel/model variant and return acceptance score within 5ms of probe completion
Telemetry events emitted for every probe: decode.probe.started, decode.probe.accepted, decode.probe.rejected, decode.fallback.invoked, decode.metrics.summary

Controlled rollout: canary at 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated abort if (1) probe_accept_rate < 60% for more than 10m or (2) quality regression > 0.5% on eval set for two consecutive 30m windows
Fallback is deterministic and preserves tokenstream order and KV-cache correctness (no missed tokens or corrupt cache across fallback boundary)
End-to-end median latency improvement meets target for canary workloads or the rollout automatically halts
design_decisions: Use a two-stage prefill probe: 1) micro-prefill (<= 8 tokens) to exercise attention kernels and KV cache behavior, 2) decode probe extension if acceptance ambiguous

Acceptance score combines: predicted token-entropy delta, kernel compatibility fingerprint (kernel_sig), and cached prefix hit-rate. We will compute a weighted score: 0.5*entropy_delta + 0.3*kernel_sig_score + 0.2*prefix_hit_rate (weights tunable via feature flag)
Fallback targets: first fallback to same model on conservative kernel (full-precision / less aggressive optimization), second fallback to larger compatible model if kernel incompatibility detected
Routing decisions made at request admission with a TTL for probe validity; if prefill takes longer than configured threshold (e.g., 25ms), operator aborts optimistic path
Telemetry schema chosen for structured events to enable high-cardinality filtering in Console metrics (see docs link below)
implementation_plan: Runtime: add OptimisticDecodeOperator component that integrates with existing scheduler and kernel-selector modules
Routing: implement lightweight router that evaluates request attributes (seq_len, prompt_token_count, model_family, kernel_fingerprint) and decides probe eligibility
Telemetry: wire structured events into internal event bus and add tagging for customer_id, route_id, probe_id
Acceptance scoring: implement in C++ hot path with a fallback to runtime-configurable scoring function (feature-flagged) for tuning
Testing: unit tests for scoring edge cases, integration tests to validate KV cache continuity across fallback, chaos tests to force fallbacks
Console: add dashboard tiles for probe_accept_rate, wasted_tokens_per_hour, fallback_rate_by_model
Rollout: implement rollout controller that enforces abort gates and canary percentages per region/customer tier
test_plan: Unit: scoring boundary conditions, kernel_sig mismatch handling, TTL expiry
Integration: end-to-end probe -> accept -> decode path on dev cluster with representative prompts
Performance: benchmark median latency and p95 with and without optimistic operator on synthetic workload and sampled traffic
Regression: run eval-suite against stable prompts and measure quality delta; failure if >0.5% regression
Chaos: induce kernel failures and assert deterministic fallback and no token duplication/corruption
monitoring_and_alerting: Console metric: decode.probe_accept_rate (1m/5m windows) with alert if <60% sustained for 10m
Console metric: decode.fallback_rate_by_model with alert if >5% for a given model over 30m
Cost metric: wasted_tokens_per_hour caused by probes (tracked separately to help tuning)
SLO monitor: end-to-end 99th percentile latency should not regress by >10% in canary (auto-abort if threshold crossed)
Incident playbook: steps to disable optimistic routing globally or per-tenant; rollback instructions and data collection checklist
notes: Trade-offs: More aggressive probes lower latency but increase wasted token cost and potential quality regressions. We start conservative and tune weights in acceptance score.
Decision rationale: Two-stage probe balances false positives (premature accept) and false negatives (needless fallback). Micro-prefill should be cheap to avoid cost blowup.
Open questions: How to best surface per-tenant cost trade-off in Console (billing vs opt-in flag)? We need PM input.
Performance concern: scoring in hot path must be <=2ms; will implement optimized C++ path and a slower JS/Go path for debugging
